title: ActorTaskCreateRequest
description: actor.task-create-request@1: the body of POST /api/v1/tasks on OpenVibe.Actor (capability actor.task.create), the creation subset of platform.task@1. TASK is the instruction in plain words. MODE is the planner objective (default balanced). BUDGET caps what this task may cost (per_task_usd) and what the caller's tasks may cost in one UTC day (per_day_usd); either may be left out for the person's free-allowance defaults, and a value above the person's tier is refused 422 actor.budget.over_tier, never silently lowered. AGENT pins one agent system by its id from GET /api/v1/agent-systems, the public catalog (routing still checks that it can take the task); AGENT_ID names one of the caller's own agent contacts from GET /api/v1/agents to run this task as (absent: Vibe, their first agent). LEVEL is the thread's approval level; the effective level is the higher of the agent's own level and this one, inherited along the person's own parent chain and never from outside work. IDEMPOTENCY_KEY: a repeat from the same requester within 24 h with an identical body answers the first task (200), with a different body 409 actor.idempotency.conflict. WEBHOOKS (at most 8): each an https URL and the state changes to deliver there (the names of platform.task@1 `state`). Actor signs every delivery with a secret it mints for the task, returned once as `webhook_secret` in the answer that created it (and in an idempotent repeat), and POSTs actor.task-webhook@1 through its egress guard: public addresses only, ports 443 or 8443, no credentials in the URL, never a redirect. A URL that cannot be delivered to is refused 422 actor.webhook.refused. A webhook may instead name a project secret (`secret_ref`, ADR-056): its deliveries are then signed by OpenVibe.Network with that secret, in the same headers, and no webhook_secret is minted when every webhook names one. A secret_ref on a task outside a project is refused 422 actor.webhook.secret_unavailable. CONVERSATION names the product conversation this task answers ({ product, id }); TOOLS names the registry tool names the run may call (an empty array answers with no tool calls; a name nothing offers is said aloud in the run, never silently dropped); MODEL names one exact model id, resolved like one the person picked themselves. All three are the one-engine slice: a product has Actor answer one turn of its own conversation.

agent.description: An agent system id from GET /api/v1/agents.

url.description: The HTTPS endpoint Actor POSTs to.

events.description: The state changes delivered; the names of platform.task@1 `state`.

secret_ref.description: The name of a project secret (ADR-056) that signs this webhook's deliveries instead of the task's own secret. The task must be made in a project (by an app or agent token carrying project_id and env); the secret is looked up in that project and environment, and the project must have granted it to actor for sign. Actor never sees the value: OpenVibe.Network computes each signature.

webhooks.description: Where Actor tells the caller about this task's state changes (plan T17).

agent_id.description: One of the caller's own agent contacts (actor.agent@1) the task runs as. Absent: their Vibe, created on first read. The public agent-system catalog stays in `agent`.

level.description: The thread's approval level. The effective level is max(the agent's level, this level, the levels of the person's own parent tasks). The always-ask floor still applies.

product.description: The product whose conversation this task answers (exchange, chat, …).

id.description: That product's key for the conversation and turn.

conversation.description: The product conversation this task answers. Stored on the task so a later query can find the turn's task; the product keeps the task id beside its own conversation.

tools.description: The registry tool names the run may call. An empty array answers with no tool calls; a name nothing offers is said aloud in the run, never silently dropped.

model.description: One exact model id, resolved by OpenVibe.AI like one the person picked themselves. Omitted: Actor answers on its default.

examples.task: Find out who runs the mail for openvibe.network and whether its SPF and DMARC are set up properly.
Summarize today's top three posts on openvibe.news.
